# extractor.sh agent documentation

> extractor.sh searches webpages, current news, openly licensed images, public videos, places, and market data, then converts known public URLs into reusable Markdown or normalized JSON through cacheable HTTP GET endpoints.

Base URL: `https://extractor.sh`

No account is required for 10 successful uncached operations per IP each UTC day. New accounts receive a one-time welcome bonus of 1,000 non-expiring credits. Signed-in homepage and platform-playground requests use the account balance automatically. External integrations use that same balance with `Authorization: Bearer ext_live_…`. One credit is committed only when a cache miss succeeds. Cache hits and errors are free. Do not put credentials, cookies, private URLs, or non-public data in request parameters.

## Hosted MCP server

Connect an MCP-compatible client to the stateless Streamable HTTP endpoint:

`https://extractor.sh/mcp`

The server exposes nine read-only tools: `extract_public_url`, `search_web`, `search_news`, `search_images`, `search_videos`, `search_places`, `search_stocks`, `get_market_movers`, and `get_market_data`. MCP and GET requests share their corresponding cache entries, anonymous allowance, prepaid metering, and rate limits. MCP clients may forward the optional Bearer key. `search_web` can restrict discovery to one hostname. `search_videos` accepts an exact creator constraint. `search_places` handles addresses, businesses, landmarks, and local categories with optional coordinate bias. `search_stocks` keeps its stable name while resolving equity or crypto asset names into market symbols. `get_market_movers` returns daily gainers, losers, or most-active equities. `get_market_data` accepts an optional quote currency, returns the public schema-v1 entity as structured content, and links a bundled line-chart resource for MCP Apps-capable chats. Other clients receive the same ordinary JSON or Markdown fallback, and the chart does not make a separate market-data request.

## Extraction endpoint

`GET /api/extract`

Query parameters:

- `url` — Required absolute public HTTP or HTTPS URL. Maximum length: 2048 characters.
- `format` — Optional. Use `json` (default) or `markdown`.
- `focus` — Optional topic from 1 to 80 characters for generic webpages.

Example Markdown request:

```sh
curl --get 'https://extractor.sh/api/extract' \
  --data-urlencode 'url=https://example.com/article' \
  --data-urlencode 'format=markdown'
```

## Search endpoint

`GET /api/search`

- `q` — Required search query. Maximum length: 200 characters.
- `limit` — Optional integer from 1 to 10. Default: 10.
- `format` — Optional. Use `json` (default) or `markdown`.
- `language` — Optional canonical BCP 47 tag. Default: `en-US`.
- `country` — Optional two-letter country. Default: `US`.
- `site` — Optional hostname restriction such as `linkedin.com`; omit the scheme and path.

```sh
curl --get 'https://extractor.sh/api/search' \
  --data-urlencode 'q=Cloudflare Workers documentation' \
  --data-urlencode 'format=json'
```

Search JSON is a schema-v1 `web-search` feed. Its ordered `document` items contain titles, public URLs, and short snippets. Use extraction on a selected URL for full page content.

## News endpoint

`GET /api/news`

- `q` — Required news query. Maximum length: 200 characters.
- `limit` — Optional integer from 1 to 50. Default: 10.
- `format` — Optional. Use `json` (default) or `markdown`.
- `language` and `country` — Optional locale controls.
- `timeframe` — Optional `any`, `1h`, `1d`, `7d`, or `30d`.

```sh
curl --get 'https://extractor.sh/api/news' \
  --data-urlencode 'q=AI infrastructure' \
  --data-urlencode 'limit=10' \
  --data-urlencode 'format=json'
```

News JSON is a schema-v1 `google-news` feed containing `article` items. Results can include public titles, publishers, publication dates, summaries, and links. Complete publisher article bodies and personalized feeds are not included.

## Image endpoint

`GET /api/images`

- `q` — Required image query. Maximum length: 200 characters.
- `limit` — Optional integer from 1 to 20. Default: 10.
- `format` — Optional. Use `json` (default) or `markdown`.
- `usage` — Optional `all`, `commercial`, `modify`, or `commercial-and-modify`.
- `orientation` — Optional `any`, `landscape`, `portrait`, or `square`.

Image JSON is a schema-v1 `image-search` feed. Document items include source pages and image media, plus creator, dimensions, description, and license metadata when available. Always follow the returned license requirements.

## Video endpoint

`GET /api/videos`

- `q` — Required video query. Maximum length: 200 characters.
- `limit` — Optional integer from 1 to 20. Default: 10.
- `format` — Optional. Use `json` (default) or `markdown`.
- `language` — Optional canonical BCP 47 tag. Default: `en-US`.
- `country` — Optional two-letter country. Default: `US`.
- `platform` — Optional `any` (default) or `youtube`. Use `youtube` when the user specifically requests YouTube results.
- `sort` — Optional `relevance` (default) or newest-first `date`. Use `date` when the user asks for the latest or newest video.
- `creator` — Optional exact creator name. Combine with `sort=date` and `limit=1` for that creator’s newest matching upload.

Video JSON is a schema-v1 `video-search` feed. Semantic `video` items contain public source-page links and available creator, publication time, displayed relative upload time, description, duration, and thumbnail metadata. For “give me the latest video of Taylor Swift,” send `q=Taylor Swift`, `creator=Taylor Swift`, `platform=youtube`, `sort=date`, and `limit=1`; the first item is the newest matching upload by that exact creator. Omit `creator` when the user wants any recent video about the subject. Safe search is strict, successful results may be cached for one hour, and direct streams or downloads are not returned.

## Place endpoint

`GET /api/places`

- `q` — Required address, business, landmark, or local-category query. Maximum length: 200 characters.
- `limit` — Optional integer from 1 to 10. Default: 5.
- `format` — Optional. Use `json` (default) or `markdown`.
- `language`, optional `country`, paired `lat`/`lon`, and `type` control localization and filtering.

Place JSON is a schema-v1 `place-search` feed. Document items can include coordinates, normalized addresses, categories, country codes, websites, phone numbers, opening hours, and canonical map links. This is submitted lookup rather than autocomplete. Results contain OpenStreetMap data and retain its required attribution.

## Finance endpoint

`GET /api/finance`

- `symbol` — Required market symbol, up to 32 supported characters.
- `timeframe` — Optional `1d`, `5d`, `1mo`, `3mo`, `6mo`, `1y`, `5y`, or `max`. Default: `1mo`.
- `quote` — Optional three-letter output currency such as `EUR`. Omit it to preserve the listing currency.
- `format` — Optional `json` (default) or `markdown`.

Without `quote`, values remain in the instrument listing currency. With `quote`, snapshot fields and chart-ready history are converted in the same operation and expose `listingCurrency`, `quoteCurrency`, `exchangeRate`, and `exchangeRateTimestamp`. The interval is selected automatically, history is capped at 512 points, and successful responses may be cached for five minutes.

`GET /api/finance/search`

- `q` — Required company or asset name, brand, or partial ticker, up to 200 characters.
- `limit` — Optional integer from 1 to 10. Default: 10.
- `instrument` — Optional `equity` (default) or `crypto`.
- `format` — Optional `json` (default) or `markdown`.

Finance search returns a schema-v1 `finance` feed containing the requested equity or crypto listings and may be cached for one hour. MCP clients use `search_stocks`, then pass the selected symbol to `get_market_data`. When a user requests a currency, pass it as `quote` to `get_market_data` instead of making a separate currency-pair call.

`GET /api/finance/movers`

- `list` — Optional `gainers` (default), `losers`, or `active`.
- `limit` — Optional integer from 1 to 10. Default: 10.
- `format` — Optional `json` (default) or `markdown`.

Market movers returns one already-ranked daily equity list with available price, daily change, percentage change, volume, range, exchange, currency, market state, and timestamp fields. Use it for “what stock rose or fell the most today?” and most-active questions; do not try to derive a market-wide ranking from company-name search. Results may be delayed and may be cached for five minutes.

Example JSON extraction request:

```sh
curl --get 'https://extractor.sh/api/extract' \
  --data-urlencode 'url=https://example.com/article' \
  --data-urlencode 'format=json'
```

## JSON response

Successful JSON responses contain:

- `schemaVersion` — Currently `1`.
- `type` — One of `document`, `article`, `product`, `post`, `profile`, `video`, `audio`, or `feed`.
- `source` — A recognized platform or provider-neutral capability such as `web`, `web-search`, `image-search`, `video-search`, `place-search`, or `finance`.
- `id` — Stable source identifier when available, otherwise `null`.
- `url` — Canonical source URL.
- `title` — Extracted title or `null`.
- `author` — Extracted author or `null`.
- `publishedAt` — ISO timestamp when available, otherwise `null`.
- `content` — Clean Markdown content.
- `media` — Public image, video, or audio references.
- `attributes` — Fields specific to the semantic entity type.
- `items` — Present for feed and profile responses; omitted for individual entities.

Each item follows the same entity shape. Product and variant `price` fields are non-negative integers in the currency's minor unit; for example, `1999` with `EUR` means €19.99. Use `priceDisplay` for presentation. Products and variants can expose SKU, GTIN, seller, category, specifications, stock state, variants, and multiple images when present. Shared nullable fields are present with `null`, while unavailable optional attributes are omitted.

Software products can additionally include `softwareVersion`, `operatingSystem`, `contentRating`, and `developerUrl` attributes.

Finance documents can include `tickerSymbol`, exchange, effective `currency`, `listingCurrency`, `quoteCurrency`, `exchangeRate`, `exchangeRateTimestamp`, quote fields, `marketState`, `historyTimeframe`, `historyInterval`, bounded `history`, and dividend or split `events`. Finance search feeds contain equity or crypto documents with the available exchange, listing currency, sector, and industry fields. Generic webpages can include `language`, `modifiedAt`, and `wordCount`; video feeds expose effective `videoPlatform` and `videoSort`, while video items can expose `publishedAtDisplay`; images, products, variants, posts, places, and feeds expose the additional optional fields documented by the JSON Schema.

Machine-readable JSON Schema: `https://extractor.sh/schemas/extraction-v1.json`

## Markdown response

With `format=markdown`, the response body is raw Markdown with `Content-Type: text/markdown; charset=utf-8`.

The public website pages also support HTTP content negotiation. Send `Accept: text/markdown` to any platform landing page to receive an agent-readable Markdown representation.

## Supported sources

### Web

Public HTTP and HTTPS articles, documentation, blogs, and other content pages. Submit the ordinary public page URL; extractor.sh handles supported pages automatically and returns a consistent response shape.

### Amazon

Public product detail pages from supported Amazon country stores return one product entity. Public search results, storefronts, Idea Lists, and explicitly shared Wish Lists return product feeds. Results can include seller, category, specifications, variants, multiple images, and integer minor-unit prices when exposed. List discovery, categories, pagination, carts, accounts, reviews, and personalized offers are not supported. Results may be cached for up to one hour.

Example: `https://www.amazon.de/product-name/dp/B09B8X9RGM`

Search example: `https://www.amazon.de/s?k=mechanical+keyboard`

### Apple App Store

Public Apple App Store app detail pages return one software product entity. Results can include the numeric app ID, name, developer, description, integer minor-unit price, ratings, version, operating-system requirement, release details, icon, and screenshots. Search, charts, reviews, accounts, and app downloads are not included. Results may be cached for up to one hour.

Example: `https://apps.apple.com/us/app/chatgpt/id6448311069`

### Bluesky

Public Bluesky profile pages return a profile entity with recent public post items. Exact public post pages return one post entity. Replies and parent threads are excluded. Profiles may omit complete embedded and quoted content.

Example: `https://bsky.app/profile/bsky.app`

Post example: `https://bsky.app/profile/bsky.app/post/3mqcp5qjdfs26`

### Google News

Public Google News search, topic, and top-stories pages return up to 50 article entities. Results can include public titles, publishers, dates, summaries, and source links. Full publisher article bodies, personalized For You results, Google Search, and Google Shopping are not included.

Example: `https://news.google.com/search?q=Cloudflare&hl=en-US&gl=US&ceid=US%3Aen`

### Google Play

Public Google Play app detail pages return one software product entity. Results can include the Android package ID, name, developer, description, integer minor-unit price, rating, category, content rating, icon, and screenshots. Search, category browsing, reviews, accounts, and APK downloads are not included. Results may be cached for up to one hour.

Example: `https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.openai.chatgpt`

### Instagram

Public Instagram post and reel pages return one post entity with exposed carousel media, dimensions, coauthors, location, partnership state, and engagement when available. Public profile pages can include verification, pronouns, an avatar, counts, and recent public post items. Private or login-only content, stories, comments, transcripts, and media downloads are unsupported.

### Mastodon

Public status pages on compatible instances return one post entity with text, author, date, content warning, and media descriptions when available. Private statuses, timelines, complete threads, and media downloads are unsupported.

Example: `https://mastodon.social/@trwnh/99664077509711321`

### Reddit

Public Reddit post pages, subreddit and community pages, and public user profile pages. Private and quarantined communities are unsupported. Post extraction does not include the complete comment tree.

Example: `https://www.reddit.com/r/CloudFlare/`

### Shopify

Public Shopify product pages return one product entity. Public storefront and collection pages return a feed with up to 50 product entities. Submit the ordinary public storefront page. Protected or unavailable storefront data may produce an incomplete result or an error.

Example: `https://store.example/products/black-shirt`

### [WooCommerce](https://extractor.sh/woocommerce/)

Public WooCommerce product pages return one product entity. Supported shop, product-search, storefront, and product-category pages return feeds with up to 50 product entities. Results can include integer minor-unit prices, availability, ratings, categories, brands, attributes, and images.

Example: `https://store.example/product/blue-shirt/`

### SoundCloud

Public tracks, playlists, and sets return an audio entity; creator pages return a profile entity. Comments, waveforms, transcripts, and media downloads are not provided.

Example: `https://soundcloud.com/forss/flickermood`

### Spotify

Public tracks, albums, playlists, podcast shows, episodes, and supported short links return an audio entity; artist pages return a profile entity. Lyrics, transcripts, playback data, audio analysis, and media downloads are not provided.

Example: `https://open.spotify.com/episode/7makk4oTQel546B0PZlDM5`

### TikTok

Public TikTok video and photo post pages return one post entity. Public creator pages return a profile entity with public counts and up to ten recent post items. Short links are supported when they resolve to one of these public pages. Private, deleted, or age-restricted content, comments, transcripts, and media downloads are unsupported.

Example: `https://www.tiktok.com/@scout2015/video/6718335390845095173`

### Vimeo

Public Vimeo video pages return one video entity with title, author, description, upload date, duration, thumbnail, and source URL when available. Transcripts, captions, comments, and media downloads are not provided.

Example: `https://vimeo.com/286898202`

### X

Public `x.com` and legacy `twitter.com` status URLs. Private, deleted, and age-gated posts are unsupported.

### [Yahoo Finance](https://extractor.sh/yahoo-finance/)

The finance API provides company-name stock search, configurable bounded history, and optional requested quote currencies. Ordinary quote and price-history URLs submitted to extraction retain a one-month daily-history default and native listing currency. Market values may be delayed or unavailable.

Example: `https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/AAPL/`

### YouTube

Public watch, Shorts, and `youtu.be` video pages, plus public channel, handle, legacy user, and playlist pages. Transcripts, captions, and media downloads are not provided.

Example: `https://www.youtube.com/@Cloudflare`

## Limits and caching

- Anonymous allowance: 10 successful uncached operations per IP per UTC day.
- New-account welcome bonus: 1,000 non-expiring credits granted once.
- General limit: 60 uncached search or extraction requests per client per 60 seconds.
- High-cost extraction limit: 5 requests per client per 60 seconds.
- Product, profile, and feed results may be cached for 1 hour.
- Yahoo Finance market documents may be cached for 5 minutes.
- Finance API responses may be cached for 5 minutes.
- Web search results may be cached for 1 hour.
- News search results may be cached for 1 hour.
- Image search results may be cached for 1 hour.
- Place search results may be cached for 1 hour.
- Map search results may be cached for 1 hour.
- Other single-entity results may be cached for 30 days.
- Maximum extracted result size: 2 MB.

Rate-limited responses use HTTP `429` and include `Retry-After` when available. Errors use a JSON object with `error.code` and `error.message`.

When a source blocks extraction or returns an upstream failure, the error message includes the upstream HTTP status when available. A `source_blocked` code means the source required authentication or denied access, commonly because of bot protection or access rules.

## Pricing

Prepaid credits cost $0.49 / 1,000 credits and never expire. Each successful uncached extraction, web search, news search, image search, video search, place or map search, or finance request counts as one credit. One-time pay-as-you-go top-ups accept exact amounts from $10.00 to $4,900.00. Optional capped automatic funding is off by default and requires separate approval. Dodo Payments provides the hosted checkout and acts as merchant of record. Usage alerts are sent at 80%, 90%, and 100% with a direct top-up link.
